description:
Bondy is an always-on, clustered router for the Web Application Messaging Protocol (WAMP).
Applications connect over WebSocket, raw TCP, HTTP long-poll, or server-sent events and use it
to call remote procedures and to publish and subscribe to events. It embeds an HTTP API gateway
that translates REST calls into WAMP operations, per-tenant identity and role-based access
control, and a cluster layer that replicates that security state across nodes. It is deployed as
a network daemon, usually as the front door between untrusted clients and internal services.

NOTE: this export describes an UNPUBLISHED ref (feature/mcp, 168 commits ahead of develop, on no
remote) plus uncommitted working-tree edits. It is not the contract for any released Bondy.
Authority order is prose > yaml > json; this file cannot be used to triage on its own.

adversaries.threshold: none. Replication is CRDT-based with no quorum, no voting, and no Byzantine tolerance; a single rogue peer with peer-plane access can inject security state.

properties_provided.conditions: forwarding headers move source_ip only from a peer inside a configured trusted_proxies CIDR; with the list unset no peer is trusted
the auth class limiter is consulted before the credential is checked; this claims consultation, not that it always answers
the default configuration of a fresh install only; not a deployment the operator has opened up
exact matches an identical URI only; prefix matches on a component boundary; wildcard is component-wise with equal component count. The EMPTY prefix matches every URI by design.
a ticket authrealm is accepted only when it equals the target realm or that realm's configured SSO realm
admin-only procedures require a master-realm session; other meta-API calls bind the realm argument to the session realm unless the session is on the master realm
the admin_local socket only; mode 0600 in a 0700 directory, and the listener refuses to start if the mode cannot be set. Other UDS listeners are NOT narrowed.

node-local: every grant and revoke invalidates this node's cached contexts and the session re-resolves on its next authorization. The 300s epoch is a backstop. The cross-node window is disclaimed separately.

THRESHOLD: super-linear work in message size, subscription count, registry size or session count on a routing/registry/decode path is a bug; a constant factor is not. Does not cover AAE work under divergence, absolute traffic volume, or work caused in a downstream system.

header NAMES and VALUES on the mail path only; not message bodies and not the other connectors. CR/LF/NUL are REJECTED, never stripped or folded. Routing and identity headers are set from the request and relay config; caller copies are refused.

Bondy-issued credentials only. JWT: rejected once iat + exp + 120s has passed, where exp is a DURATION not an RFC 7519 NumericDate, and the leeway EXTENDS validity. Ticket: rejected once expires_at is within 120s of now, where the leeway SHORTENS validity. No nbf is issued or checked.

covers every credential comparison. CRA and SCRAM call compare/2; stored passwords use crypto:hash_equals/2 directly; cryptosign and tokens delegate to Ed25519 and jose verify_strict. compare/2 answers false on unequal lengths rather than raising. Fixed 2026-08-30 - both CRA and SCRAM previously hand-compared.

GIVEN HONEST REPLICAS. Merge is commutative, idempotent under redelivery, and convergent for the supported cell types. Does not cover the reclamation-versus-in-flight-read interaction (Q17), nor a Byzantine participant.

registrations and subscriptions keyed by the ref session id; registrations are removed BEFORE promises are flushed so a concurrent CALL cannot pick a departing callee. Cluster broadcast is suppressed; other nodes learn by replication.

PER-REPLICA only. Strictly increasing 64-bit value that never regresses across backwards system-clock jumps, repeated same-millisecond calls, or peer events from clocks ahead. Logical overflow clamps and advances physical rather than wrapping. Says nothing about agreement BETWEEN replicas - see clock-skew.
a session is created only on the success branch; the error clause never reaches bondy_session_manager:open/3. Out-of-order messages stop the connection rather than mutating state.

mops is the umbrella app apps/mops as of 2026-08-30, no longer an external git dep tracked on {branch, master}. Verified: 34 apply_op clauses, no erlang:apply / list_to_atom / binary_to_atom, one binary_to_existing_atom that cannot mint atoms, unknown operators raise invalid_expression.

reclamation runs inside the applier, the sole writer, so a discard cannot interleave with an apply to the same cell; the overlay fence discards a cell only when nothing is pending for its key. The strict boundary keeps a tombstone whose HLC equals the stability point.

per-session state is process-local. Bondy is NOT share-nothing: the projection (single writer), the HLC (atomics + compare_exchange), the registry (ETS) and the rate-limit buckets (ETS) are deliberately shared and are OUTSIDE this property. A race inside one of those is a real finding.

no bound on skew BETWEEN replicas and no rejection of a far-future peer timestamp. A far-future stamp wins last-writer-wins indefinitely, so on a security cell a later honest write cannot overwrite it. Reaching that needs peer-plane access, already excluded by the adversary model. Per-replica monotonicity is claimed as hlc-monotonic. Rests on a STATED limit.
issued JWTs and tickets; Bondy neither issues nor checks nbf, so a token is usable from the moment it is signed. Rests on a STATED limit.

properties_not_provided.reason: covers ONLY the cross-node window: another node honours the old grant until replication reaches it, bounded by the 300s context epoch. Invalidation on the writing node is immediate and is claimed as revocation-invalidation. A revocation unhonoured on the writing node, or still honoured after the epoch, routes VALID. Rests on a STATED limit.

downstream_responsibilities: bind the peer port to a private interface, or enable cluster TLS with verify_peer and a private cluster CA; TLS without verify_peer does not discharge this
set security.admin_user.password before first boot, and the same value on every node of a cluster
leave security.allow_anonymous_user at local unless anonymous access from the network is intended
never run a production realm with security_enabled false; it disables authentication and RBAC for that realm
when proxy_protocol is enabled set trusted_proxies to the balancer CIDRs, so per-source attribution and IP-scoped credential sources remain meaningful
if client mTLS is relied on, set fail_if_no_peer_cert on; verify_peer alone only requests a certificate
a subscriber that was disconnected does not receive what it missed; use a broker bridge or an application store for durability
configure security.master_key if realm signing keys must be encrypted at rest
put a hard limiter in front of Bondy if a real request ceiling is required; the built-in limiter fails open
multiply a realm total budget by node count to get the cluster-wide ceiling
validate call arguments in the callee; Bondy does not inspect payloads
escape routed payloads for the consuming sink before rendering, logging, or querying
treat API-specification authorship as control-plane authority; a spec author chooses each endpoint's security scheme and any forward target
the transport enforces a frame or length cap; a deployment needing a smaller bound sets it at the listener
clients must name an existing realm in HELLO
non-standard WAMP options are underscore-prefixed and declared
restrict the admin listener and the admin unix socket to trusted operators

known_misuse.pattern: following the README quick-start's DELETE /realms/{uri}/security_enabled step on a realm that then carries real traffic
known_misuse.why_unsafe: It short-circuits authorization entirely: bondy_rbac:authorize/3 returns ok without checking any grant, so every default-deny guarantee is void for that realm.
known_misuse.instead: create users, groups, and grants and leave security enabled; treat the quick-start realm as disposable

known_misuse.pattern: binding the Partisan peer port to 0.0.0.0 or routing it over a shared network to join distant nodes
known_misuse.why_unsafe: The peer plane is unauthenticated and plaintext by default. It carries replicated credentials and realm signing keys, and there is no quorum to outvote a rogue peer.
known_misuse.instead: use a bridge relay, which is cryptosign-authenticated and per-realm, and keep the peer plane on one private network

known_misuse.pattern: enabling proxy_protocol while leaving trusted_proxies empty, collapsing every request onto the balancer's address
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Not a spoofing hole, since Bondy ignores forwarding headers from untrusted peers. The failure is quieter: every request is attributed to the balancer, collapsing per-source rate limiting and IP-scoped credential sources onto one address.
known_misuse.instead: set trusted_proxies to the balancer CIDRs, and mode strict if requests without proxy information should be dropped

known_misuse.pattern: setting a realm total rate limit expecting it to bound the whole cluster
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Buckets are node-local, so the real ceiling is the configured total multiplied by node count, and the limiter fails open on top of that.
known_misuse.instead: divide the intended cluster ceiling by node count, and enforce hard ceilings upstream

known_misuse.pattern: branching or alerting on rate-limit refusals as though they were permission denials
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Rate limiting is capacity policy, not authorization. A refusal means later, not no.
known_misuse.instead: branch on the WAMP not_authorized error for permission; treat 429 as transient backpressure

known_misuse.pattern: one prototype realm supplying groups and grants to realms belonging to different tenants
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Inherited grants cross the realm boundary by design, weakening tenant isolation for every realm that inherits.
known_misuse.instead: keep a prototype realm within a single trust domain

known_misuse.pattern: setting tls.verify to verify_peer on a client listener and leaving fail_if_no_peer_cert off, believing client certificates are required
known_misuse.why_unsafe: verify_peer alone only requests a client certificate. A client presenting none still completes the handshake, so an authentication control the operator believes is mandatory is in fact optional.
known_misuse.instead: set fail_if_no_peer_cert on alongside verify_peer, and confirm a certificate-less client is refused

known_misuse.pattern: an API specification whose forward action builds its target URL from request-supplied values
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Bondy issues the outbound request. The target is meant to carry operator authority, not request data.
known_misuse.instead: keep forward targets static in the specification

known_non_findings.reported_as: binary_to_term/1 called without [safe] in bondy_oplog_crdt_* decode_state/1 or the compaction checkpoint decode/1
known_non_findings.why_safe: Covers only the f8-storage-at-rest component(s), and only the unsafe-deserialization-atom-exhaustion symptom. Discharged by own-bytes-rule. Outside those components or that symptom this entry does not apply and the report must be triaged normally.
known_non_findings.suppression: the sink is a decode_state/1 or checkpoint decode/1 in those modules; the bytes decoded were written by this node; and the report does not demonstrate a path by which peer-shipped or client-shipped bytes reach that call. If that last condition fails it is a real finding and routes VALID.

known_non_findings.reported_as: rand:uniform/1 used to generate a session identifier at bondy_session_id.erl:54
known_non_findings.why_safe: Covers only the f1-session-protocol component(s), and only the weak-prng-predictable-identifier symptom. Discharged by session-id-entropy. Outside those components or that symptom this entry does not apply and the report must be triaged normally.
known_non_findings.suppression: the sink is bondy_session_id:new/0 at line 54; the claim is that the FULL session id is guessable; and the report does not identify a mechanism treating the 56-bit external id alone as a secret or capability. If that last condition fails it is a real finding, because the external id is public by construction.
